steps.what: 26. Every hook is a virtual no-op on AbstractModel (returning Task.CompletedTask or the unmodified value), so the dispatcher calls EVERY listener unconditionally and 'does not implement' equals 'implements as identity' (AbstractModel.cs:199-2440)
steps.rationale: The sim dispatches duck-typed -- `if hasattr(l, '<hook>')` (hooks.py:62 and the same line in all 66 dispatchers), stated as intentional in the module docstring ('Dispatch is duck-typed: a hook only calls listeners that define a matching method'). The observable is identical whenever the method names agree, because a C# no-op override and an absent Python method both contribute nothing; the only difference is a maintenance one (a misspelled hook name is a silent no-op in the sim and a compile error in C#), which is why test/test_hook_order.py's `trace` helper raises AttributeError on an unknown hook name.

steps.what: 31. Additive (num += item.ModifyXAdditive(target, num, ...)) and multiplicative (num *= item.ModifyXMultiplicative(target, num, ...)) are SEQUENTIAL chains in which each listener receives the RUNNING value and the dispatcher folds the result in immediately, in decimal (Hook.cs:1320-1337 ModifyBlock, 2515-2538 ModifyDamageInternal)
steps.issue: gap G9 (parallel sum/product vs sequential running-value chain). The sim hands EVERY additive/multiplicative listener the same pre-step base and aggregates the returns afterwards (hooks.py:52-64 sum, 66-78 product, 98-109, 111-122), then the caller applies the aggregate once (cmds.py:57-58 damage, 145-147 block). SETTLED ON THE MERITS BY EXECUTION in the fix pass, in three parts. (1) The base-vs-running ARGUMENT is inert: no implementation on either side reads the value the dispatcher hands it -- `py tools/audit/dormancy_probes.py cs-running-value` finds 0 of the 46 C# ModifyDamage/BlockAdditive/Multiplicative overrides (and 0 of the 9 Enchant* ones) reading their running-value parameter, and `sim-running-value` finds 0 of the sim's 31 implementations reading theirs. (2) For the ADDITIVE family the two shapes are therefore exactly equal: base + sum(a_i) == (((base + a1) + a2) + ...) over integers, 0 mismatches in an exhaustive sweep. (3) For the MULTIPLICATIVE family they are NOT equal as the sim implements them, because the sim multiplies the factors together in float FIRST and applies the product once, while C# folds each factor into the running decimal. LIVE and executed: with Shrink (x0.7, dealer-side, applied by the ported Act-1 Shrinker Beetle monsters/overgrowth/shrinker_beetle.py:39-40 and by the Shrink Potion potions.py:718-722, powers.py:1366-1387) on the player and Vulnerable (x1.5, target-side, powers.py:403-417) on the enemy, a 20-damage powered attack deals 20 in the sim and 21 in the game (sim: 1.5*0.7 = 1.0499999999999998, 20 * that = 20.999999999999996, int -> 20; game: 20m*1.5m = 30m, 30m*0.7m = 21m). Base 40 diverges the same way. A control run that keeps the sim's float arithmetic but threads it sequentially returns 21, so the divergence is the AGGREGATION SHAPE, not float-vs-decimal representation. Because the outcome can and does differ, this is a gap, not a deliberate-divergence. SAME MECHANISM, SAME VERDICT AT EVERY SITE (rule 3): audits/seam/damage_pipeline.json guard N3 is the damage site and was raised from deliberate-divergence to gap in this same pass with the same evidence; the BLOCK site (Hook.cs:1320-1337 vs hooks.py:98-122 + cmds.py:145-147) is creature_card_cmds' step 13, AMENDED (fix pass 2): it carries the identical gap, but is DORMANT there -- all five ported block multipliers return only {0.0, 0.75, 2.0}, every one dyadic, and an exhaustive sweep of 15 ordered subsets x bases 0-999 found 0 mismatches between the sim's product and C#'s sequential decimal. A non-dyadic block multiplier would make it live; the only one in the source is MultiplayerScalingModel.cs:52-68, waived under N1.md's cross-seam section. Pinned here by test/test_hook_order.py::TestHookDispatchOrder::test_multiplicative_damage_modifiers_chain_sequentially (strict xfail).

guards.what: N2 -- presentation and modding: InvokeExecutionFinished / the ExecutionFinished event (step 22) and the ModHelper.IterateAll*Subscribers tails (steps 13, 17).

ModHelper is the mod-loading extension point and the sim has no mod loader. Neither can change a single-player outcome.

guards.what: N3 -- CombatHistory is a sim-only listener, registered first (combat.py:111-112) so it observes every event before any relic or power. The game has no history listener: CombatManager.History is written by explicit calls (CardModel.cs:1930, 1956), not through the hook system.
guards.rationale: The observable is identical: CombatHistory only records, never mutates combat state, and registering it first is what makes the recording complete by the time a later listener reads it (relics/paels_eye.py:27-34 scans it; a grep for `combat.history` over sts2_rl finds 9 reader modules in all -- paels_eye, powers.py and seven card modules. FIX-PASS CORRECTION: the first pass named relics/whispering_earring.py as the second reader and it reads no history at all). Routing the recording through the listener list instead of through explicit call sites is a sim re-architecture with no behavioural consequence -- verified by reading every CombatHistory hook method, all of which only append entries.

guards.what: N4 -- Modifiers and BadgeModels as listeners (step 10; RunState.cs:573-574, CombatState.cs:470-477).
guards.rationale: Modifiers are custom/daily-run mutators loaded from save.Modifiers (RunState.cs:296, 344) and a standard run has none. BadgeModels ARE cloned into every run (RunState.cs:332), but BadgeModel.cs:3-9 states they exist to 'keep track of stats for badges' and an executed grep over src/Core/Models/Badges/ finds no badge overriding any Should*/Modify*/TryModify* hook -- they subscribe to events for meta-progression accounting only. Out of scope for the same reason ascension values are, and unable to change an in-run outcome even if they were in scope.

guards.what: N5 -- the run/combat delegation split: in combat a run-level dispatch visits deck cards first and then the whole combat list (steps 14-18), and the sim has two disjoint dispatch systems instead (HookSystem inside a combat, duck-typing over run.relics outside one).
guards.issue: gap N5 (no run-level listener list): RunState.cs:545-596 makes every deck card and its enchantment a run listener at all times, in combat and out, and delegates to the combat list when there is a child combat. The sim has no run-level HookSystem: run-scoped hooks are duck-typed directly over run.relics (relics/base.py:205-235) and a deck card is never a listener. DORMANT, evidence executed: the same `dormancy_probes.py card-hooks` scan (203 card classes x 66 hook names) finds no sim card class implementing a run-scoped hook at all -- the six it implements are all combat hooks. Concrete trigger: porting any CardModel that overrides AfterRoomEntered/AfterRewardTaken/ShouldAddToDeck or another run-level hook.

guards.what: N6 -- AbstractModel.ShouldReceiveCombatHooks (AbstractModel.cs:53-62) is abstract and 19 model classes override it, but a whole-source grep for reads finds ZERO consumers; the real filtering is structural (which lists IterateHookListeners walks) plus Contains.
guards.rationale: Documented-but-unread property. The sim has no counterpart and needs none: it performs the same filtering structurally, by choosing what to register. Recorded so a future reader does not mistake it for a missing gate. Executed: `grep -rn ShouldReceiveCombatHooks --include=*.cs .` over the whole decompiled tree returns only the abstract declaration and the 19 overrides, no reads.

guards.what: N7 -- character scope: the OrbQueue listener block (step 8; CombatState.cs:448) and the orb-shaped dispatchers this record owns that go with it (ModifyOrbValue 1874, ModifyOrbPassiveTriggerCount 1855, AfterOrbChanneled 844, AfterOrbEvoked 858, AfterModifyingOrbPassiveTriggerCount 784).
guards.rationale: Orbs are the Defect's mechanic. The sim implements one character, the Ironclad, so there is no orb queue to place in the listener order and no orb listener whose position could be wrong. This is a CHARACTER-scope exclusion of the same kind as ascension values -- not multiplayer, which is why it no longer sits under N1. It becomes a real ordering question only if a second character is ported, at which point the slot is between PotionSlots and the cards (CombatState.cs:436-449) and gap G2 already covers getting it wrong.
